line: First interview at Brightline for Head of Growth

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Hi Matt, thanks for making the time today.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thanks for having me, I'm glad we could make it work.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, loud and clear.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Great. So I'll give you a quick overview of the role, and then we'll get into your background.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: We're a dental services group with about forty locations, and paid media has been mostly agency-run until now.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: So, tell me a little bit about yourself.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Sure. I've spent about ten years in performance marketing, most recently running paid media for multi-location healthcare brands.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The work I'm proudest of is rebuilding a dental group's paid search account.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Okay, interesting.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Walk me through that rebuild. What did you actually change?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: When I came in, about sixty percent of spend was going to branded search, so I'll start there.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: We restructured the account around three service lines and cut cost per lead from two hundred twelve dollars to one thirty one.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: That makes sense to me.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: And how did you measure whether that actually worked?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: We tracked booked appointments, not just form fills, and I'll be honest, that took a quarter to get right.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Right, okay, got it.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: I'm curious how you think about attribution when the reports disagree.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I usually start by lining up the attribution windows, because that explains most disagreements.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Yeah, we've been burned by that. Our last agency reported on a thirty day window and finance used seven.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Let's switch gears a little.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a stakeholder. How did you handle it?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: A founder wanted to double the social budget after one good week. I asked for two more weeks of data and we'll see, I said, whether it holds.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: It didn't hold, and we kept the budget where it was.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Ha, that's a familiar story.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Okay, great. So how would you approach the first ninety days here.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: First month I'd audit the account and tracking. Second month I'd rebuild campaign structure. Third month I'd start testing.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: And what would you need from us to make that work?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Access to the booking data, and one person on your side who can make decisions quickly.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: That should be fine. I'll connect you with our ops lead if we move forward.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Explain how you'd handle it if we asked you to cut the budget in half.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'd protect the campaigns that book appointments and pause the rest, then show you what we lose.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Makes sense.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: What's your biggest weakness?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I can stay in the details too long, so I've learned to set a deadline for the analysis and then decide.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Salary expectations?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm looking for something in line with a head of growth role, and I'm flexible on structure.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Okay. We'll come back to that later in the process.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: I think that's most of what I had. We're at time, so do you have any questions for us?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes. What would make someone successful in this role in the first year?

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Honestly, getting the tracking fixed and making the board trust the numbers.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: That's helpful. And what are the next steps?

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: I'll talk to the team this week and we'll get back to you by Friday.

turns.speaker: Them
turns.text: Let's see, I think that's everything. Thanks again, Matt.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you, I'll send over the case study I mentioned by tomorrow.
